entries.built: Initialised a local Git repository, connected it to a GitHub remote, and configured Netlify to auto-deploy from the main branch — portfolio now goes live on every push

entries.concept: Understanding the deployment pipeline under pressure
entries.built: Explained the full commit-push-deploy relay from memory, reasoned correctly through a GitHub failure scenario, and distinguished clearly between Claude Code, Git, GitHub and Netlify

capabilityReports.sessionFocus: Git version control and Netlify deployment pipeline
capabilities: I can initialise a Git repository from scratch using git init and make a first commit
I can connect a local project to a GitHub remote and push files with git push
I can link Netlify to a GitHub repository so every push auto-deploys the live site
I understand the difference between building with Claude Code and deploying with git push — and that Claude Code can run the git commands itself
I understand that progress.json is the data layer that connects my learning to my live portfolio
gaps: Explore git branching and pull requests in a future session

capabilityReports.sessionFocus: Git, GitHub and Netlify — the deployment pipeline
capabilities: I can explain the full journey of a change from my local computer to a live website — commit, push, deploy — and describe what each step does and why
I can reason through failure scenarios in the pipeline — for example, knowing that a GitHub outage after a commit but before a push leaves the live site unchanged but the local files safe

I can clearly distinguish between Claude Code (the agent that runs commands), Git (the system that stores snapshots), GitHub (the cloud copy), and Netlify (the publisher that watches GitHub and rebuilds the site)
gaps: Stay conscious of saying 'Claude Code did it' when the precise answer is 'Claude Code told Git to do it'
